findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name Path traversal from command-line arguments
 * @description File operations with paths from argparse or command-line without proper validation
 * @kind path-problem
 * @problem.severity high
 * @id py/path-traversal-cli
 * @tags security
 *        external/cwe/cwe-022
 */

import python
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.DataFlow
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.TaintTracking
import semmle.python.ApiGraphs
import semmle.python.Concepts

module PathTraversalConfig implements DataFlow::ConfigSig {
  predicate isSource(DataFlow::Node source) {
    exists(DataFlow::AttrRead attr |
      attr.getAttributeName() in ["dest", "name", "path", "dir", "directory", "output"] and
      source = attr
    )
  }

  predicate isSink(DataFlow::Node sink) {
    exists(DataFlow::CallCfgNode call |
      (
        call = API::moduleImport("pathlib").getMember("Path").getACall() or
        call = API::moduleImport("os").getMember("makedirs").getACall() or
        call = API::moduleImport("os").getMember("mkdir").getACall() or
        call = API::moduleImport("shutil").getMember(["copy", "copytree", "move", "rmtree"]).getACall() or
        call = API::builtin("open").getACall()
      ) and
      sink = call.getArg(0)
    )
  }
}

module PathTraversalFlow = TaintTracking::Global<PathTraversalConfig>;
import PathTraversalFlow::PathGraph

from PathTraversalFlow::PathNode source, PathTraversalFlow::PathNode sink
where PathTraversalFlow::flowPath(source, sink)
select sink.getNode(), source, sink, "Potential path traversal from $@.", source.getNode(), "user input"
findings.hypothesis: Path traversal vulnerability where command-line arguments flow to file operations without proper validation

/**
 * @name Symlink following vulnerability
 * @description Creating symlinks or following symlinks without proper validation can lead to unauthorized file access
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity warning
 * @id py/symlink-following
 * @tags security
 *        external/cwe/cwe-59
 */

import python
import semmle.python.ApiGraphs

from DataFlow::CallCfgNode call
where
  call = API::moduleImport("os").getMember(["symlink", "link", "readlink"]).getACall() or
  call = API::moduleImport("pathlib").getMember("Path").getReturn().getMember("symlink_to").getACall() or
  call = API::moduleImport("shutil").getMember("copytree").getACall() and
  exists(DataFlow::Node arg |
    arg = call.getArgByName("symlinks") and
    arg.asExpr().(BooleanLiteral).booleanValue() = true
  )
select call, "Symlink operation that may be vulnerable to symlink attacks."
findings.hypothesis: Check for symlink operations that could be exploited for unauthorized file access

findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name Insecure HTTP URL usage
 * @description Using HTTP URLs for downloading packages or resources can allow MITM attacks
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity warning
 * @id py/insecure-url
 * @tags security
 *        external/cwe/cwe-319
 */

import python
import semmle.python.ApiGraphs

from Expr url
where
  exists(StrConst s |
    s = url and
    s.getText().regexpMatch(".*http://.*") and
    not s.getText().regexpMatch(".*localhost.*") and
    not s.getText().regexpMatch(".*127\\.0\\.0\\.1.*") and
    not s.getText().regexpMatch(".*://example.*")
  )
select url, "Insecure HTTP URL found: " + url.(StrConst).getText()
findings.hypothesis: Looking for hardcoded HTTP URLs that could expose the application to man-in-the-middle attacks

message.text: Insecure HTTP URL found: Gets the short path name of a given long path - http://stackoverflow.com/a/23598461/200291.
